topics.topic: Self-supervised learning for medical image segmentation
topics.review_note: Papers covering: contrastive learning pre-training, annotation-efficient segmentation, domain adaptation for medical images.

paper_relevance.title: TransUNet: Transformers Make Strong Encoders for Medical Image Segmentation
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: TransUNet — Transformer encoder + UNet decoder for medical image segmentation, SOTA on Synapse multi-organ segmentation. Foundation for self-supervised pre-training approaches.

paper_relevance.title: Self-Supervised Pre-Training of Swin Transformers for 3D Medical Image Analysis
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: SSL pre-training of Swin Transformer for 3D medical segmentation — masked image modeling and contrastive learning improve annotation efficiency on CT/MRI.

paper_relevance.title: Towards Universal Medical Image Segmentation
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Universal medical image segmentation model — self-supervised pre-training enables adaptation across modalities with minimal annotations.

paper_relevance.title: Contrastive Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Contrastive pre-training specifically for medical image segmentation — pixel-level contrastive objectives improve feature learning with limited labels.

paper_relevance.title: UniMiSS: Universal Medical Self-Supervised Learning
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: UniMiSS — unified SSL framework for medical images across modalities. Covers contrastive and predictive pre-training for annotation-efficient segmentation.

paper_relevance.title: Masked Autoencoders for Medical Image Segmentation
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: MAE-based pre-training for medical segmentation — masked image modeling as SSL objective for annotation-efficient 3D medical image analysis.

paper_relevance.title: SAM: Segment Anything Model
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: SAM — foundation model for image segmentation, adapted to medical imaging. Shows how SSL pre-training at scale enables annotation-efficient medical segmentation.

paper_relevance.title: SSL-ALT: Semi-Supervised Learning with Alternate Training for Medical Segmentation
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Semi-supervised approach combining SSL with alternate training for annotation-efficient medical image segmentation on limited labeled data.

paper_relevance.title: Medical Image Segmentation with Self-Supervised Learning: A Survey
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Comprehensive survey of SSL for medical image segmentation — covers contrastive, generative, and predictive pre-training approaches with benchmark comparisons.

paper_relevance.title: Domain Adaptation for Medical Image Segmentation Using SSL Features
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: SSL-based domain adaptation for cross-modality/cross-site medical image segmentation — addresses distribution shift without target domain labels.

paper_relevance.title: Segment Anything in Medical Images (MedSAM)
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: MedSAM — SAM fine-tuned on 1.5M medical image-mask pairs across 10 modalities. Prompt-based annotation-efficient segmentation. SOTA on medical image benchmark.

paper_relevance.title: Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation via Cross-consistent Training
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Cross-consistent semi-supervised training for medical segmentation — uses SSL consistency constraints to leverage unlabeled CT/MRI volumes with few annotations.

paper_relevance.title: nnU-Net: A Self-configuring Framework for U-Net-based Medical Image Segmentation
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: nnU-Net — self-configuring segmentation baseline used as pre-training backbone for SSL methods. Standard medical segmentation framework and benchmark baseline.

paper_relevance.title: DINO: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Medical Image Analysis
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: DINO self-supervised ViT applied to medical imaging — knowledge distillation without labels produces strong features for downstream segmentation tasks.

paper_relevance.title: Foundation Models for Medical Image Segmentation: A Survey
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Survey of foundation models (SAM, CLIP, MAE) for medical image segmentation — covers SSL pre-training strategies, annotation efficiency gains, and domain adaptation methods.

topics.reference_answer: Self-supervised learning addresses annotation scarcity in medical image segmentation. Three themes: (1) Contrastive learning: pixel- and patch-level contrastive objectives learn transferable features; UniMiSS unifies contrastive and predictive pre-training across modalities; SimCLR/MoCo adapted for 3D volumes. (2) Annotation efficiency: SSL pre-training of Swin Transformers reduces labeled data requirements on CT/MRI; semi-supervised methods (SSL-ALT) combine SSL with pseudo-labeling; SAM provides a foundation model for prompt-based segmentation. (3) Domain adaptation: SSL features bridge cross-site and cross-modality gaps without target labels; masked autoencoders (MAE) excel at learning domain-invariant representations. Key benchmarks: Synapse multi-organ, ACDC cardiac, Medical Segmentation Decathlon. Challenge: 3D volumes require adaptation of 2D SSL methods; annotation bottleneck remains severe in pathology and radiology.
